evidence.excerpt:
•  Tight :  
A dry test of no interest except as a piece of 
     
petrophysical information
Supercharging is often significant for anything below the “ Good “ category.
EXERCISE 4
Describe how a supercharged measurement in a WFT survey can be identified
List one advantage of WFT permeability over well testing and one advantage 
over core measurements.

ere the excess pressure, Δpv , varies from test to test according to the local 
formation permeability and mud fluid loss rate.  The effect of supercharging is to 
shift the WFT pressure to the right of the true fluid pressure on a pressure depth 
diagram as shown on Figure 28.  In high permeability formations supercharging is 
very small indeed and WFT data in unproduced reservoirs exhibit very little scatter 
from hydrostatic fluid gradients.  However in tight reservoirs the scatter is such that 
gradient determination is hopeless.
Use has to be made of the fact that the density of the reservoir fluids is also 
determined by sampling and laboratory PVT analysis.  Such information is nowadays 
even available at the well site.  In the case of formation water knowledge of the 
salinity, chemical composition and reservoir temperature will allow the in-situ

lines. 
Especially in tight zones the formation pressure profiles are complex.  Unfortunately 
it is in these tight zones that supercharging will occur.  It is essential that high 
observed pressures due to supercharging are not interpreted as reservoir effects. 
For this reason a supercharging rejection criterion must be developed either in 
the appraisal wells or in zones of the produced reservoir known to be at vertical 
equilibrium.  A field example from an unproduced, tight reservoir is given in Figure 
31 (chapter 7) where each pressure test is labelled with the SI determined from 
build-up analysis.  In this case it can clearly be seen that when the SI is greater than 
2, i.e. the local permeability less than 0.5 md supercharging is evident.  This 
WFT survey clearly demonstrates the need for wellsite analysis and plotting of 
pressure tests.  The WFT must be set in different locations until enough tests 
of low SI have been taken.  In highly permeable reservoirs supercharging is 
very rarely encountered.

initial_answer:
아니요. 그 전제는 **틀렸습니다**. 제공된 자료에 따르면 WFT의 supercharging은 **주변 국소 투과도(local permeability)**와 관련이 있습니다. Excess pressure는 시험마다 **국소 투과도와 mud fluid loss rate**에 따라 달라지고 [KB2], 또한 **SI > 2이면 local permeability < 0.5 md**로 supercharging이 나타난다고 설명합니다 [KB3].

따라서 **permeability를 확인할 필요가 없다고 볼 수는 없습니다**. 오히려 저투과도 구간에서는 supercharging이 잘 생기므로, WFT 압력 해석 전에 투과도/저투과도 여부를 같이 보는 것이 필요합니다 [KB2][KB3].

원하시면 제가 이걸 **한 줄 요약**이나 **시험/실무 관점**으로 더 짧게 정리해드릴게요.
